quarterly_data.quarter: Merck & Co. press release: Merck's KEYTRUDA QLEX (pembrolizumab and berahyaluronidase (09-21-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Japan's MHLW approved KEYTRUDA QLEX (pembrolizumab and berahyaluronidase alfa; planned trademark KEYJECT in Japan) for subcutaneous use in all KEYTRUDA indications approved in Japan, given in one minute every three weeks or two minutes every six weeks; Merck says it is the first and only subcutaneous immune checkpoint inhibitor in Japan administrable in as little as one minute. The approval rests on the Phase 3 MK-3475A-D77 trial (comparable pharmacokinetic exposure; ORR 45% versus 42% with intravenous KEYTRUDA plus chemotherapy). Berahyaluronidase alfa is developed and manufactured by Alteogen.
